Before you start

First you\'ll hear a few chords played one after another. A chord is several notes sounding together. Their job is to set up a \"home\" note — the one everything else gets compared to. The last chord lands back on home, so home is the sound you\'re left with.
Then, after a short gap, you\'ll hear one single note on its own.
That single note is the question. Your job is to say where it sits compared to home.

You answer with the buttons at the bottom. Right now there are three: \"1\" is home itself, and \"3\" and \"5\" are the two other notes from that opening chord — a little above home, and higher still.

That last note was \"%1$s\".
It was home itself — the note the chords settled on.
It sits above home, and you can hear it leaning against home rather than resting on it.
You won\'t always be sure, and that\'s expected. Guessing is how this gets easier — nothing is scored and nothing is held against you.
